housing.name: Should the government build significantly more homes
housing.text: Should the government actively intervene in the housing market to significantly increase the supply of new homes?

yes.text: Should the government prioritize building social and council housing over providing incentives for private developers?
Should the central government have the power to impose mandatory building targets on local councils, even if those councils object?
Should the government be allowed to override local planning rejections for projects deemed "nationally significant"?
Should the government establish a state-owned construction company to build these homes directly?

no.text: Should the government provide direct grants to local authorities to set up their own municipal building departments?
Should local communities be given a legal right to a "community share" of the revenue generated by new developments?

yes.text: Should these community funds be strictly ring-fenced for local infrastructure like schools and GP surgeries?

no.text: Should residents have a final vote on the specific architectural style and density of new developments in their area?
Should the government reform the "Green Belt" to allow for new housing on land that is currently protected?

yes.text: Should the government simplify the planning process to allow for "automatic approval" of projects meeting environmental standards?
Should there be a total ban on legal challenges from local interest groups for developments on released Green Belt land?

no.text: Should developers be required to provide a minimum of 50% affordable housing on any land released from the Green Belt?
Should the government focus exclusively on "Brownfield" sites, even if this increases the time and cost of construction?

yes.text: Should the government provide massive tax breaks to developers who take on the risk of decontaminating old industrial land?

no.text: Should the government implement a "land value tax" to force owners of empty urban plots to develop them?
Should the government focus on reducing the demand for housing rather than trying to increase the supply?

yes.text: Should the government significantly limit net migration as the primary tool for reducing housing pressure?
Should the government also restrict the number of international students who are allowed to rent in high-demand cities?
Should universities be legally required to provide on-campus housing for all international students they enroll?

no.text: Should the government prioritize housing for British citizens over non-citizens in both the social and private sectors?
Should the government increase taxes on second-home owners and "buy-to-let" investors to free up existing stock?

yes.text: Should there be a total ban on foreign nationals who do not live in the UK from purchasing residential property?

no.text: Should local councils be allowed to charge triple the standard rate of Council Tax on properties left empty for six months?
Should the market be the sole regulator of housing through the total removal of price caps and rent controls?

yes.text: Should the government abolish the current planning system entirely and replace it with a simple zoning model?
Should developers be allowed to build high-rise apartments in any urban area without a height restriction?

no.text: Should the government remove all "affordable housing" requirements for developers to speed up delivery?
Should the government focus on financial reforms, such as making it easier for banks to lend to first-time buyers?

yes.text: Should the government act as a guarantor for mortgages for those who cannot afford a traditional deposit?

no.text: Should the government offer tax-free savings accounts where every pound saved for a deposit is matched by the state?

housing.name: Should renters have stronger legal protections
housing.text: Should the law grant tenants significantly more legal rights and security than they currently possess?

yes.text: Should the government introduce a permanent cap on how much a landlord can increase rent each year?
Should rent increases be strictly tied to local average wage growth rather than inflation?
Should the government establish a "National Rent Board" with the power to freeze rents in housing emergency areas?
Should the government compensate landlords if a rent freeze makes their mortgage repayments unaffordable?

no.text: Should it be illegal for a landlord to sell a property while a tenant is in the middle of a long-term lease?
Should tenants have a legal right to "rent-to-buy," where a portion of rent goes toward a future down payment?

yes.text: Should the government mandate that all large-scale institutional landlords offer rent-to-buy options?

no.text: Should the state provide tax breaks to landlords who offer tenants the first option to buy at a discount?
Should it be almost impossible for a landlord to evict a tenant who is paying rent and looking after the property?

yes.text: Should the "right to a pet" be an absolute legal requirement that landlords cannot refuse?
Should tenants be required to take out "pet insurance" as a condition of this right?

no.text: Should the government set a maximum "pet deposit" that is higher than the standard limit?
Should landlords be allowed to evict tenants if they can prove they need the property for a family member?

yes.text: Should there be a "transparency register" where landlords must prove the family member actually moved in?

no.text: Should landlords be required to pay for the tenant's relocation costs if they are evicted for landlord-use?
Should the government prioritize protecting the rights of landlords to manage their property freely?

yes.text: Should "no-fault" evictions be reinstated to give landlords more flexibility in managing their portfolios?
Should the notice period for a no-fault eviction be kept at two months rather than being extended?
Should the government speed up the court process for evicting tenants in significant rent arrears?

no.text: Should the government provide temporary housing for any tenant evicted through no fault of their own?
Should the government focus on reducing the taxes that landlords pay to encourage them to stay in the market?

yes.text: Should mortgage interest relief be fully restored for all private landlords?

no.text: Should landlords be exempt from energy-efficiency requirements if the costs would lead to a rent hike?
Should the government rely on a "voluntary code of conduct" for landlords rather than passing new laws?

yes.text: Should the government offer a "quality mark" to good landlords that allows them to charge higher rents?
Should this quality mark be independently audited by a panel including tenant representatives?

no.text: Should landlords who refuse to join the voluntary code be barred from government-backed insurance?
Should the government leave the relationship between landlord and tenant entirely to the individual contract?

yes.text: Should the state still provide a free "small claims" court to resolve basic contract disputes?

no.text: Should there be a mandatory "standard contract" that every landlord and tenant must use?

housing.name: Should the government prioritise getting more people onto the housing ladder
housing.text: Should increasing the rate of homeownership be a primary goal of government policy?

yes.text: Should the government provide direct financial subsidies to help first-time buyers with their deposits?
Should these subsidies be limited to people who have lived in their local area for at least five years?
Should the government also provide low-interest loans for the remaining portion of the house price?
Should the government have a "share" in the future profit of the home when the owner eventually sells?

no.text: Should these loans be automatically written off if the owner works in a public service role for ten years?
Should the government prioritize subsidies for people who are currently living in social or council housing?

yes.text: Should the "Right to Buy" scheme be expanded to include all housing association tenants?

no.text: Should the government prevent anyone who has previously owned a home from accessing these subsidies?
Should the government abolish Stamp Duty entirely for anyone buying a home to live in?

yes.text: Should the government recoup the lost tax revenue by increasing taxes on commercial property developments?
Should there be a permanent ban on converting commercial offices into residential flats?

no.text: Should the government instead increase the "annual tax on enveloped dwellings" for luxury homes?
Should the government focus on "Shared Ownership" schemes where people buy a percentage of a home?

yes.text: Should the government cap the service charges that shared owners pay to prevent them being "trapped"?

no.text: Should "Shared Ownership" be replaced by a "Help to Build" scheme for individuals to build their own homes?
Should the government focus on making long-term renting a stable and attractive alternative to owning?

yes.text: Should the law be changed to allow tenants to stay in their rented homes for ten years or more?
Should tenants be allowed to make permanent changes to their rented home, such as redecorating?
Should landlords be required to pay tenants back for the value added to the property?

no.text: Should tenants be legally required to restore the home to its original state before they move out?
Should the government provide "tenant-friendly" pensions where the state matches contributions?

yes.text: Should this be funded by a new levy on developers who build high-end luxury apartments?

no.text: Should the government instead provide a "housing allowance" for all non-homeowning pensioners?
Should the government focus on building more social housing for everyone, regardless of income?

yes.text: Should social housing be "tenure blind," meaning it looks identical to private market housing?
Should high-income people in social housing pay a "fair market rent" to subsidize their neighbors?

no.text: Should the government sell off social housing in expensive areas to fund more homes in cheaper areas?
Should the government remain neutral and stop giving tax breaks or subsidies to either owners or renters?

yes.text: Should the government use the money saved to simply build more infrastructure like roads?

no.text: Should the government introduce a "wealth tax" on the value of all homes above a certain threshold?

defence.name: Should the UK spend significantly more on its military
defence.text: Should the UK increase its annual defence spending to at least 2.5% of GDP immediately?

yes.text: Should the increased funding be used primarily to expand the number of frontline troops?
Should the UK government aim to return the size of the regular army to over 100,000 personnel?
Should the government consider a form of limited "national service" or incentives for the reserves?
Should national service be mandatory for all 18-year-olds, with a choice of military or community roles?

no.text: Should the government offer full university tuition fee waivers for anyone who serves five years?
Should the military focus on "home defence," such as protecting UK waters, rather than overseas missions?

yes.text: Should a dedicated "Home Guard" or civil defence force be established for domestic emergencies?

no.text: Should the UK withdraw its troops from permanent bases in the Middle East to focus on Europe?
Should the majority of new funding be spent on high-tech capabilities like AI, drones, and cyber-defence? \[13, 16\]

yes.text: Should the government prioritize buying this technology from UK-based companies, even if it is more expensive?
Should the government take a direct ownership stake in critical defence firms to prevent foreign sales?

no.text: Should the UK share its most advanced cyber-defence technology with all its NATO allies?
Should the UK purchase "off-the-shelf" military equipment from the US to ensure value for money?

yes.text: Should the UK move toward an arsenal that is perfectly compatible with the US military?

no.text: Should the UK join a "European Defence Fund" to develop new weapons systems with the EU?
Should the UK maintain its current budget but redirect it to prioritize diplomacy and international aid?

yes.text: Should the UK commit to spending the same on international development as it does on the military?
Should aid be used specifically to build stability in countries where conflict leads to migration?
Should the military be given a secondary role in delivering aid in those countries?

no.text: Should aid be withheld from countries that do not support UK foreign policy at the UN?
Should the UK focus its diplomatic efforts on leading a "global disarmament" movement?

yes.text: Should the UK become a leading advocate for a global ban on fully autonomous weapons?

no.text: Should the UK significantly reduce its role in NATO to signal a more neutral foreign policy?
Should the UK focus on "economic security" by building domestic industry instead of military power?

yes.text: Should the UK restrict foreign investment in sectors like energy to protect national security?
Should the government have the power to block any foreign takeover of a "strategic" UK company?

no.text: Should the UK prioritize trade with democratic allies over autocracies, even if it hurts the economy?
Should the UK rely on "collective security" through the UN while gradually reducing its independent capability?

yes.text: Should the UK surrender its independent seat on the UN Security Council to a shared "European" seat?

no.text: Should the UK focus its military entirely on special forces and niche roles for allies?

defence.name: Should the UK seek to rejoin the European Union
defence.text: Should the UK's long-term goal be to rejoin the European Union as a full member?

yes.text: Should the UK accept that it would no longer have "opt-outs" from the Euro or Schengen?
Should the UK commit to adopting the Euro as its currency within a decade?
Should the UK hand over control of interest rates and monetary policy to the European Central Bank?
Should the UK also support a "European Treasury" with the power to tax citizens directly?

no.text: Should the UK retain the right to veto any changes to EU-wide tax rules?
Should the UK join the Schengen Area, removing passport controls at EU borders?

yes.text: Should the UK abolish the "Common Travel Area" with Ireland to comply with full Schengen rules?

no.text: Should the UK be allowed to temporarily close its borders during high migration?
Should the UK refuse to rejoin unless it is guaranteed its previous "special status" and rebate?

yes.text: Should the government hold a second referendum only after final terms are fully negotiated?
Should the referendum require a "super-majority" of 60% for a lasting decision?

no.text: Should the UK rejoin only if a majority in every UK nation (Eng, Scot, Wal, NI) vote YES?
Should the UK pursue "Associate Membership" with market access but no vote on rules?

yes.text: Should the UK be willing to pay a large annual fee for this status?

no.text: Should the UK still be required to allow free movement of workers as part of this status?
Should the UK remain outside the EU but seek a much closer relationship?

yes.text: Should the UK rejoin the EU Single Market while staying out of the political union?
Should the UK accept all EU regulations on goods to ensure frictionless trade?
Should the European Court of Justice be the final judge of UK compliance?

no.text: Should the UK have a "right to diverge" even if it leads to new trade barriers?
Should the UK join an EU Customs Union to remove border checks?

yes.text: Should the UK give up its right to sign independent trade deals with the US?

no.text: Should the UK only join the customs union for certain sectors like food?
Should the UK focus on building trade ties with the US and India instead of the EU? \[20, 21\]

yes.text: Should the UK prioritize a trade deal with the US, even if it means US food standards?
Should the UK allow US companies to bid for contracts to run NHS services?

no.text: Should the UK align its environmental laws with the US rather than the EU?
Should the UK focus on "CANZUK" ties with Canada, Australia, and New Zealand?

yes.text: Should there be free movement of people between the UK and these three countries?

no.text: Should the UK act as a "global hub" for free trade by removing all its own tariffs?

defence.name: Should the UK keep its nuclear weapons
defence.text: Should the UK maintain and renew its independent nuclear deterrent, Trident?

yes.text: Should the UK remain dependent on the US for the maintenance of its nuclear missiles?
Should the UK increase its contribution to the US-led development of next-generation warheads?
Should the UK have a formal "veto" over any US decision affecting UK readiness?
Should the UK pay a higher premium to the US to ensure this veto is legally binding?

no.text: Should the UK be required to support US foreign policy as a condition of support?
Should the UK seek to build more missile components itself to reduce "cut-off" risks?

yes.text: Should the government spend £10 billion on a domestic factory for missile maintenance?

no.text: Should the UK's nuclear subs be placed under a joint "NATO Command" to share the burden?
Should the UK develop its own entirely sovereign nuclear missile system, regardless of cost?

yes.text: Should the UK also develop its own satellite guidance system for its nuclear forces?
Should the UK partner with France to create a "European Nuclear Shield"?

no.text: Should the UK increase its taxes to pay for this multi-decade project?
Should the UK reduce its nuclear fleet from four submarines to three to save money?

yes.text: Should the UK accept that it might not have a submarine at sea 100% of the time?

no.text: Should the UK move its nuclear weapons from submarines to land-based silos?
Should the UK unilaterally disarm its nuclear weapons and use the savings for conventional forces?

yes.text: Should the roughly £3 billion annual running cost be redirected exclusively into the NHS? \[17, 22\]
Should the government also sell the nuclear submarine fleet to an ally to recoup money?
Should the money from the sale be used to pay off part of the national debt?

no.text: Should the UK allow US nuclear submarines to use UK ports after it has disarmed?
Should the savings be used to build a "world-leading" conventional military?

yes.text: Should the UK focus on building a massive fleet of aircraft carriers?

no.text: Should the UK focus on being a global leader in peace-keeping instead?
Should the UK pursue "multilateral disarmament"—only getting rid of weapons if others do?

yes.text: Should the UK set a firm "deadline year" for when it will start disarming?
Should the UK stop its current renewal program as a sign of good faith?

no.text: Should the UK offer to reduce its warhead count by 50% for a treaty with Russia?
Should the UK replace nuclear weapons with advanced "non-nuclear" strategic weapons?

yes.text: Should these weapons be designed to destroy an enemy's command center only?

no.text: Should the UK rely entirely on the "US Nuclear Umbrella" for its protection?

economy.name: Should the richest people pay significantly more in tax
economy.text: Should the government significantly increase the total tax burden on the top 1% of earners and wealth holders?

yes.text: Should the government introduce a "Wealth Tax" on the total value of assets rather than just income?
Should the wealth tax apply to assets worth over £5 million? \[12, 25\]
Should the tax be an annual 1% levy rather than a one-off payment? \[24, 25\]
Should the government have the power to seize assets if the owner cannot pay in cash?

no.text: Should the tax rate be higher for "non-productive" assets like luxury art?
Should the wealth tax apply to everyone with assets over £1 million, including their home?

yes.text: Should there be an exemption for anyone who has lived in their home for 30 years?

no.text: Should the government use the revenue to fund a permanent cut in income tax?
Should the government instead increase the top rate of Income Tax to 50% or higher?

yes.text: Should the threshold for the top rate be lowered so it hits more professionals?
Should the government also remove the personal allowance for those over £100,000?

no.text: Should the government increase taxes on "non-doms" even more than planned?
Should the government focus on equalizing Capital Gains Tax with Income Tax?

yes.text: Should the "main residence" exemption be removed for homes worth over £2 million?

no.text: Should there be a "Departure Tax" for any wealthy person who moves abroad?
Should the government focus on making the UK attractive to investors by keeping taxes low?

yes.text: Should the government prioritize cutting Corporation Tax to encourage business?
Should the UK aim to have the lowest Corporation Tax rate in the G7?
Should the government create "Special Economic Zones" with zero tax for startups?

no.text: Should the government fund these cuts by reducing civil service headcounts?
Should the government focus on simplifying the tax code rather than raising rates?

yes.text: Should the government abolish the "carried interest" loophole for private equity?

no.text: Should the government replace most taxes with a single "Flat Tax"?
Should the government prioritize reducing the national debt before any tax changes?

yes.text: Should any "windfall" tax revenue be automatically used to pay down debt?
Should the government be legally barred from running a budget deficit?

no.text: Should the government sell off more state-owned land to pay down debt?
Should the government focus on reducing "Government Waste" first?

yes.text: Should an independent auditor have the power to veto wasteful spending projects?

no.text: Should the government implement a total freeze on new public sector hiring?

economy.name: Should the minimum wage rise significantly above inflation
economy.text: Should the statutory minimum wage be raised to a level that guarantees a "real living wage"?

yes.text: Should the minimum wage be the same for all ages (abolishing lower rates for young people)?
Should the minimum wage be increased even if it leads to higher prices for consumers?
Should the government provide direct subsidies to small businesses to help them pay?
Should these subsidies be funded by a new tax on companies that use robots?

no.text: Should the government instead reduce National Insurance for small employers?
Should the minimum wage vary by region, with a higher rate for expensive cities?

yes.text: Should local mayors have the power to set their own "city minimum wage"?

no.text: Should the government implement "sector-specific" minimum wages?
Should the government keep lower rates for 16-21 year olds to encourage hiring?

yes.text: Should the gap between the youth rate and the adult rate be gradually narrowed?
Should the government provide free training vouchers for those on the youth wage?

no.text: Should the youth rate be abolished for anyone with over two years of experience?
Should the minimum wage be replaced by a "Universal Basic Income" (UBI)?

yes.text: Should the UBI be high enough to live on without any other source of income?

no.text: Should the UBI be funded by abolishing all other welfare benefits?
Should the government avoid large increases to prevent job losses and business closures?

yes.text: Should the minimum wage be strictly tied to productivity growth?
Should an independent panel of economists have the final say on the rate?
Should the panel be required by law to prioritize "business competitiveness"?

no.text: Should the government be allowed to freeze the wage during a recession?
Should the government focus on "in-work benefits" to top up low wages instead?

yes.text: Should the "taper rate" be reduced so people keep more of their benefits?

no.text: Should the government cap the total amount of benefits any household can receive?
Should the government focus on increasing "worker power" through unions?

yes.text: Should every workplace with over 50 employees be required to have a union?
Should unions have a legal right to "sector-wide bargaining"?

no.text: Should it be illegal for a company to fire a worker for taking part in a strike?
Should the government focus on "profit-sharing" where workers own a stake?

yes.text: Should this apply to all companies, including small family businesses?

no.text: Should workers be given a mandatory 10% ownership stake in their company?

economy.name: Should major public services be brought into public ownership
economy.text: Should the government nationalize major utilities and services such as water, energy, and rail?

yes.text: Should the government prioritize nationalizing the water companies as the first step?
Should shareholders be compensated based on the "market value" of their shares?
Should the government borrow money to pay for this, even if it increases debt?
Should the government be allowed to use "pension fund assets" to help fund it?

no.text: Should the government instead implement a "windfall tax" on water firms to pay for the buyout?
Should the government only pay back the "original investment" made by shareholders?

yes.text: Should the government prioritize compensating UK pension funds over foreign ones?

no.text: Should the government be prepared to fight legal challenges in international courts?
Should the government prioritize nationalizing the energy "Big Six"?

yes.text: Should the government set a "flat price" for energy that is the same for everyone?
Should the government provide free solar panels for every home?

no.text: Should the state-owned energy company be barred from making any profit?
Should the government focus on the railways, creating "Great British Railways"?

yes.text: Should the government prioritize lowering ticket prices even if it requires subsidy?

no.text: Should rail workers be banned from striking once the industry is public?
Should the government use tougher regulation and fines instead of nationalisation?

yes.text: Should regulators have the power to "ban" companies from paying dividends?
Should this dividend ban be automatic if service targets are missed?
Should the government be able to fire the CEO of a private utility?

no.text: Should companies that repeatedly fail targets be "forcibly sold" at a discount?
Should the government introduce "consumer-led" regulation where customers vote?

yes.text: Should every utility board have seats for "elected customer representatives"?

no.text: Should the government allow community-owned cooperatives to compete?
Should the government focus on increasing competition by making it easier for new firms?

yes.text: Should the government break up monopolies (like water regions) into smaller areas?
Should customers be able to switch their water supplier as easily as their phone?

no.text: Should the government subsidize "start-up" energy companies to help them compete?
Should the government sell off its remaining stakes in all services, including the Post Office?

yes.text: Should the money be used to fund a one-off "tax holiday" for everyone?

no.text: Should the government retain a "Golden Share" to prevent foreign takeovers?

healthcare.name: Should the NHS receive significantly more funding, even if taxes rise
healthcare.text: Should the government significantly increase NHS funding, even if it requires an increase in Income Tax?

yes.text: Should the extra funding be "ring-fenced" so it can only be spent on medical staff?
Should a portion of the money be strictly allocated to Mental Health?
Should the government set a legal maximum waiting time for all mental health referrals?
Should the government pay for private treatment if the NHS wait time is exceeded?

no.text: Should mental health services be delivered in schools rather than hospitals?
Should the government prioritize "Cancer Care" as the primary recipient of funds?

yes.text: Should the UK aim to have the highest cancer survival rates in the world?

no.text: Should the government prioritize "Prevention" (anti-obesity) over "Cure" (scanners)?
Should the government allow the NHS to spend the money on modernizing technology first?

yes.text: Should the NHS move toward a "digital first" model where appointments are online?
Should the government provide free tablets for elderly patients to access digital care?

no.text: Should every patient have the legal right to an in-person appointment within 48 hours?
Should the new funding be used to "nationalize" social care and make it free?

yes.text: Should social care workers be given the same pay as NHS nurses?

no.text: Should the government implement a "social care levy" on everyone over 40?
Should the NHS achieve significant "efficiency savings" before any new money is granted?

yes.text: Should the government appoint a "Efficiency Tsar" with the power to close hospitals?
Should hospitals compete for funding based on patient satisfaction scores?
Should the best hospitals be allowed to pay their staff "performance bonuses"?

no.text: Should the government centralize all NHS purchasing into a single National Body?
Should the government focus on reducing the number of "middle managers" by 50%?

yes.text: Should the saved money be used to directly increase junior doctor pay?

no.text: Should the government replace most administrative roles in the NHS with AI?
Should the UK move away from the tax-funded model toward an insurance system?

yes.text: Should the government mandate that everyone who can afford it must buy private insurance?
Should the state still provide free "emergency care" for everyone?

no.text: Should the state provide "vouchers" for low-income people to buy insurance?
Should the government introduce "small charges" for services like £10 for a GP visit?

yes.text: Should there be a total exemption for children and pensioners?

no.text: Should the revenue from these charges be kept by the local GP surgery?

healthcare.name: Should private companies be allowed to deliver NHS-funded care
healthcare.text: Should the NHS continue to use private companies to deliver medical treatments to its patients?

yes.text: Should there be a "profit cap" on how much a private company can make from an NHS contract?
Should the cap be set at 5% of the total contract value?
Should any profit above the cap be "reinvested" directly back into the local NHS?
Should the government prioritize contracts with "not-for-profit" companies?

no.text: Should private firms be barred from marketing their NHS services to the public?
Should the government allow higher profits for companies with "shorter wait times"?

yes.text: Should these companies be allowed to hire staff directly from the NHS?

no.text: Should the government implement a "staff levy" on private firms that hire NHS doctors?
Should private companies be allowed to prioritize "simpler" cases to clear backlogs?

yes.text: Should the NHS be required to pay the same "flat fee" to a private firm as it costs in-house?
Should the private firm be liable for any follow-up care if complications occur?

no.text: Should the NHS "rent out" its operating theaters to private firms on weekends?
Should private firms be legally required to take a "representative mix" of cases?

yes.text: Should the government provide "bonus payments" for treating the most complex patients?

no.text: Should the government be allowed to fine firms that refer difficult patients back?
Should the government ban all "for-profit" companies from clinical care for NHS patients?

yes.text: Should this ban also include out-of-hours GP services and pharmacies?
Should the government spend the billions needed to bring all these into state ownership?
Should the government prioritize this over reducing the elective surgery backlog?

no.text: Should the government allow "worker-owned cooperatives" to deliver these instead?
Should the government focus on building "NHS-only" diagnostic hubs?

yes.text: Should these hubs be open 24/7 to ensure the most efficient use of equipment?

no.text: Should the government allow private firms to provide "non-clinical" services like cleaning?
Should the government focus on creating "public-private partnerships" for new hospitals?

yes.text: Should the private firm be required to provide all initial capital investment?
Should the private firm own the building for 30 years before handing it to the state?

no.text: Should the NHS have the right to "buy out" the private partner at any time?
Should the government allow patients to "top up" their NHS care by paying for a private room?

yes.text: Should the "top-up" revenue be split 50/50 between the NHS and the provider?

no.text: Should this be banned to prevent a "two-tier" system where the rich get better surroundings?

healthcare.name: Should assisted dying be legal for people who are terminally ill
healthcare.text: Should it be legal for terminally ill adults to seek medical assistance to end their own life?

yes.text: Should the eligibility be limited strictly to people with six months or less to live?
Should two independent doctors be required to confirm the prognosis?
Should a High Court judge also have to sign off on every individual case?
Should the government provide a "free legal advocate" for every patient in court?

no.text: Should the "reflection period" between the request and the act be at least 14 days?
Should "intolerable suffering" be the primary criteria rather than time until death?

yes.text: Should the law also apply to people with chronic, incurable non-terminal conditions?

no.text: Should the government allow "advance directives" for those who get dementia?
Should the doctor be allowed to "object on the grounds of conscience" and refuse?

yes.text: Should the doctor be legally required to refer the patient to a colleague who will?
Should the government establish a "National Assisted Dying Service"?

no.text: Should a doctor's refusal be kept confidential to protect them from pressure?
Should the act of ending the life be done by the patient themselves (e.g., a pill)?

yes.text: Should the patient be allowed to do this at home rather than in a clinic?

no.text: Should the government provide "assisted dying suites" in hospitals?
Should the government focus on significantly increasing funding for "Palliative Care" instead?

yes.text: Should the government fund enough so that every person can choose to die at home?
Should hospices be fully funded by the state rather than charity?
Should hospice workers be given the same pay as specialist consultants?

no.text: Should the government implement a "palliative care tax" to fund this?
Should the government prioritize "pain management" research over other sciences?

yes.text: Should the government allow currently illegal drugs (like psychedelics) for end-of-life?

no.text: Should it be a crime to take a loved one to a country where assisted dying is legal?
Should the government maintain the current law because of the risk of pressure on the vulnerable?

yes.text: Should the government launch a national campaign to promote the "value of life"?
Should the government provide a "caregiver allowance" equal to the minimum wage?

no.text: Should the government be allowed to censor online content encouraging suicide?
Should the government wait for a "National Citizens' Assembly" to decide?

yes.text: Should the results of the Citizens' Assembly be legally binding on Parliament?

no.text: Should the government instead hold a "non-binding" referendum?

technology.name: Should AI systems be regulated by law before they can be released to the public
technology.text: Should the government pass new laws requiring AI models to be safety-tested before release?

yes.text: Should the UK's AI laws be "aligned" with the European Union's AI Act?
Should certain "high-risk" AI (like facial recognition in public) be banned entirely?
Should the ban also include AI that uses "emotion recognition" in workplaces?
Should the government be allowed to use these in "exceptional" national security cases?

no.text: Should there be a "private right of action" where individuals can sue for banned AI use?
Should the government establish a Central AI Regulator with power to levy large fines?

yes.text: Should the regulator also have the power to order the deletion of an unsafe AI model?

no.text: Should the government prioritize the transparency of AI over "trade secrets"?
Should the UK create its own unique, "light-touch" rules to attract AI companies?

yes.text: Should the government provide "tax credits" for any AI company moving to the UK?
Should the government also provide "sovereign computing" power for UK startups?

no.text: Should AI companies be exempt from certain data laws if training for "public good"?
Should the government focus on "liability" laws—making developers responsible for harm?

yes.text: Should this liability be "strict," meaning the company is responsible even if unintentional?

no.text: Should there be a "mandatory insurance fund" that all AI companies must pay into?
Should AI companies be allowed to "self-regulate" through voluntary codes of conduct?

yes.text: Should the government only intervene if an AI system is proven to cause physical harm?
Should the government focus on "educating the public" about AI risks instead of laws?
Should "AI Literacy" be a mandatory subject in the national school curriculum?

no.text: Should the government require all AI-generated content to have a digital watermark?
Should the government use "Sandboxes" to test AI without rules in controlled environments?

yes.text: Should the government share the results of these tests with the public?

no.text: Should companies in the sandbox be "immune" from lawsuits for mistakes during the test?
Should the government use "existing laws" (like GDPR) to govern AI instead of new ones? \[36, 40\]

yes.text: Should the Information Commissioner (ICO) be given larger fines to handle AI cases?
Should the ICO be able to "audit" the private training data of any AI company?

no.text: Should the government prioritize "human-in-the-loop" rules for AI decisions?
Should the government focus on "international treaties" rather than national laws?

yes.text: Should the UK push for a "Global AI Agency" similar to the IAEA?

no.text: Should the UK be willing to "unilaterally slow down" AI if others refuse safety rules?

technology.name: Should people have stronger legal rights over how their personal data is used
technology.text: Should the government grant individuals significantly more legal control over their personal data?

yes.text: Should people have a legal "Right to Erasure" that is absolute (meaning no exceptions)?
Should this right include "derived data," such as the patterns an AI has learned about you?
Should companies be required to "retrain" AI models if a certain number of people delete data?
Should the government subsidize the cost of this retraining for small businesses?

no.text: Should it be illegal for companies to charge users a "fee" for exercising this right?
Should the government implement a "Data Portability" rule to move digital history to rivals?

yes.text: Should this apply to all social media posts, photos, and messages?

no.text: Should the government create a "National Data Bank" for users to lease their data?
Should individuals have the right to "sell" their own personal data for a profit?

yes.text: Should there be a "minimum price" for different types of data (e.g., health vs. browsing)?
Should the government take a 10% tax on all data sales to fund services?

no.text: Should it be illegal for a company to require data as a condition of service?
Should the government focus on "Data Minimization"—collecting only the bare minimum?

yes.text: Should companies be required to delete all user data after twelve months?

no.text: Should "biometric data" (face scans) be banned from being stored on company servers?
Should the government keep current GDPR laws to avoid placing costs on the digital economy?

yes.text: Should the government make it easier for companies to share data for research?
Should the government create a "Safe Harbor" for sharing anonymized data?
Should this data be made available for "free" to UK universities?

no.text: Should the government allow companies to "auto-enroll" users into sharing?
Should the government prioritize "National Security" over individual data privacy?

yes.text: Should the intelligence services have a "backdoor" into encrypted messaging apps?

no.text: Should it be illegal for companies to use "end-to-end encryption"?
Should the government "weaken" current laws to help the UK compete in AI?

yes.text: Should UK companies be exempt from "opt-out" rules when training large models?
Should the government provide a "legal shield" for companies that leak non-sensitive data?

no.text: Should the government prioritize innovation in the official mission of the ICO?
Should the government focus on "Global Standards" rather than a unique UK law?

yes.text: Should the UK automatically accept the data laws of any trade-deal country?

no.text: Should the UK rejoin the EU's "Data Adequacy" framework?

technology.name: Should social media platforms be legally responsible for harmful content on them
technology.text: Should social media platforms be held legally liable for the harmful content posted by their users?

yes.text: Should the liability include content that is "legal but harmful" (e.g., self-harm content)?
Should platforms be required to use "AI moderation" to proactively remove this content?
Should the government have the power to "audit" these algorithms for bias?
Should the results of these audits be made public, including what topics are suppressed?

no.text: Should platforms be fined even if their AI makes a mistake and deletes "safe" content?
Should platforms be required to have human moderators review every reported post?

yes.text: Should these moderators be required to be based in the UK?

no.text: Should there be a "24-hour limit" for platforms to remove harmful content?
Should platforms only be liable for "illegal" content (e.g., terrorism, fraud)?

yes.text: Should the government publish a "definitive list" of illegal content for platforms?
Should platforms be allowed to host "hateful" content that isn't a crime?

no.text: Should executives face "prison time" if their company repeatedly fails to remove content?
Should "anonymous accounts" be banned to make it easier to prosecute individuals?

yes.text: Should everyone be required to upload a "Government ID" to open an account?

no.text: Should platforms be required to "unmask" users only if a court order is issued?
Should platforms be treated like "phone companies"—only responsible for the service?

yes.text: Should the government focus entirely on "prosecuting the individuals" who post?
Should the police have a "dedicated social media unit" in every local force?
Should the government increase the "maximum sentence" for online trolling?

no.text: Should it be illegal for a platform to "ban" a user for a legal political opinion?
Should the government rely on "user tools" (like blocking) to manage harm?

yes.text: Should the government provide a "safety rating" for every platform?

no.text: Should platforms be required to provide a "chronological feed" only?
Should the government prioritize "Free Speech" over all other concerns?

yes.text: Should the UK adopt a "First Amendment" law making it impossible to censor speech?
Should this law prevent private companies from having their own community standards?

no.text: Should the government abolish the "Online Safety Act" entirely?
Should the government focus on "Media Literacy" so people recognize harm themselves?

yes.text: Should the government fund a national "Digital Fact-Checking" service?

no.text: Should the government set up an "Ombudsman" for those wrongly banned?

education.name: Should university tuition fees be abolished
education.text: Should the government abolish tuition fees and make university education free for all UK students?

yes.text: Should the lost revenue be replaced by a new "Graduate Tax"?
Should the graduate tax be set at 2% for everyone who has a degree?
Should the tax apply even to those who have already paid off their old loans?
Should the revenue be "ring-fenced" specifically for university research?

no.text: Should the tax be higher for graduates of high-earning subjects like medicine?
Should the graduate tax be "time-limited" (e.g., you only pay for 25 years)?

yes.text: Should the tax be removed for any graduate who works in the UK public sector?

no.text: Should the tax also apply to international graduates who stay in the UK?
Should the government fund universities directly from general taxation?

yes.text: Should the government cap the total number of university places to control costs?
Should the government decide which subjects get funding based on economic needs?

no.text: Should universities be allowed to charge "top-up fees" to wealthy students?
Should an "Employer Levy" be introduced where companies pay for every graduate hired?

yes.text: Should the levy be higher for large multinationals than for small businesses?

no.text: Should the government provide "maintenance grants" to all students for living costs?
Should the current system of "fees and loans" be maintained but with better terms?

yes.text: Should the government lower the interest rate on student loans to 0%?
Should the government also increase the income threshold for repayments?
Should any outstanding debt be forgiven after 20 years?

no.text: Should the government allow parents to "buy out" their children's loans?
Should the government reintroduce "Maintenance Grants" for low-income families?

yes.text: Should these be funded by a new tax on "international student fees"? \[47, 48\]

no.text: Should the grant be tied to the "local cost of living" in the university city?
Should the government allow universities to charge "market-rate" fees with no cap?

yes.text: Should the government still provide loans to cover these higher fees?
Should the government prioritize loans for STEM subjects?

no.text: Should universities be required to provide a money-back guarantee on jobs?
Should the government replace most 3-year degrees with "1-year vocational intensives"?

yes.text: Should these intensives be fully funded by the industry they serve?

no.text: Should these intensives be delivered in the workplace rather than on campus?

education.name: Should private schools lose their charitable status and tax benefits
education.text: Should the government remove all remaining tax advantages from private schools?

yes.text: Should the extra tax revenue be "strictly ring-fenced" to hire state school teachers?
Should the government use the money to "equalize" per-pupil funding?
Should the government set a legal "maximum class size" of 15 for primary schools?
Should the government also provide free after-school tutoring for every child?

no.text: Should the government prioritize state schools in the most deprived 10% of areas?
Should the government use revenue for "means-tested vouchers" for private schools?

yes.text: Should private schools be required to accept a minimum of 20% voucher students?

no.text: Should the government instead fund "national breakfast clubs" for all?
Should private schools keep charitable status if they share their facilities?

yes.text: Should there be a "mandatory partnership" where private teachers work in state schools?
Should this be a condition for being allowed to call themselves charities?

no.text: Should the government provide tax credits for private schools that sponsor academies?
Should the government focus on "phasing out" private education entirely?

yes.text: Should it be illegal for any new private school to open in the UK?

no.text: Should the government only ban "selective" private schools?
Should the government recognize the "burden" private schools take off the state system?

yes.text: Should the government "reimburse" private schools for children with Special Needs?
Should the government allow private schools to bid for specialist state-funded hubs?
Should these hubs be open to all local children for free?

no.text: Should the government allow parents to deduct fees from their income tax?
Should the government focus on improving state schools so nobody wants to pay?

yes.text: Should the government introduce "merit-based pay" for state teachers?

no.text: Should the government replace the Ofsted system with "peer-review"?
Should the government keep the current system (including 20% VAT) but no further changes?

yes.text: Should the government monitor the impact on state school capacity for five years?
Should the government compensate councils if classes become overcrowded?

no.text: Should the government allow "low-fee" private schools to be exempt from VAT?
Should the government focus on "vocational training" rather than this debate?

yes.text: Should every private school be required to offer a technical route?

no.text: Should private schools be allowed to become state academies if they abolish fees?

education.name: Should vocational training be funded and valued equally to academic education
education.text: Should technical and vocational qualifications receive the same level of funding and status as a degree?

yes.text: Should the government replace the UCAS system with a single portal for both routes?
Should schools be "legally required" to spend equal time on vocational career advice?
Should the government abolish A-Levels and replace them with a "National Baccalaureate"?
Should the Baccalaureate be split 50/50 between academic and practical skills?

no.text: Should all "top-tier" universities be required to accept vocational qualifications?
Should the government provide a "Universal Apprenticeship Guarantee" for 18-year-olds?

yes.text: Should the government pay the full salary of an apprentice for their first year?

no.text: Should the government use the "International Student Levy" to fund this?
Should the government "fund the learner" with a Lifelong Learning Account?

yes.text: Should the account be worth £30,000 to cover three years of any training?
Should individuals be allowed to top up their account tax-free?

no.text: Should the account be replenished every ten years?
Should the government prioritize "Industry-Led" training designed by businesses?

yes.text: Should businesses be allowed to "issue their own degrees"?

no.text: Should the government give tax breaks to firms that train their own staff?
Should the government accept that degrees are more valuable for high-growth sectors?

yes.text: Should the government "reduce funding" for low-value degrees and move it to colleges?
Should "low-value" be defined by the average salary of graduates after five years?
Should the government force universities to close courses failing salary targets?

no.text: Should the government exempt "creative" degrees from these salary-based rules?
Should the government focus on upskilling the existing workforce instead?

yes.text: Should the government provide "paid training leave" for all workers?

no.text: Should the government implement a "skills tax" on firms hiring from abroad?
Should the government focus on "Work-Based Learning" rather than qualifications?

yes.text: Should the government allow people to "test out" of degrees by passing an exam?
Should these exams be provided for free by the state?

no.text: Should the government encourage "blind hiring" where degrees aren't listed?
Should the government focus on "STEM" only, reducing funding for all "soft" subjects?

yes.text: Should the government provide interest-free loans only for STEM training?

no.text: Should the government create a "National Skills Academy" for technical standards?

climate.name: Should the UK stick to its legally binding net zero targets
climate.text: Should the UK maintain its legally binding commitment to reach "Net Zero" by 2050?

yes.text: Should the government move the target "forward" to 2040 for global leadership?
Should the government ban the sale of all new "gas boilers" by 2030?
Should the government provide a "full grant" for every household to switch?
Should the grant be funded by a new "carbon tax" on all non-renewable energy?

no.text: Should the government be allowed to "fine" owners who refuse insulation?
Should the government prioritize "decarbonizing the grid" before home heating?

yes.text: Should the government build a new generation of Small Modular Nuclear Reactors?

no.text: Should the government take a direct ownership stake in all new wind farms?
Should the government prioritize "economic growth" over the speed of transition? \[3, 54\]

yes.text: Should the government "pause" green taxes during high inflation or recession?
Should the government compensate green firms if subsidies are cut?

no.text: Should the government focus on "Carbon Capture" rather than reducing use?
Should the government implement a Carbon Border Tax on imports from non-green countries?

yes.text: Should the UK use the revenue to fund green exports to developing nations?

no.text: Should the UK be willing to start a trade war with China to defend this tax?
Should the UK scrap the "Net Zero" target entirely and focus on adaptation?

yes.text: Should the government spend the billions saved on massive sea defenses?
Should the government prioritize protecting major cities over rural coastlines?
Should the government provide "relocation grants" for areas not protected?

no.text: Should every coastal council be given a "veto" over any abandonment plan?
Should the government focus on bio-engineering crops for a hotter climate?

yes.text: Should the government allow "Gene Editing" in all UK agriculture?

no.text: Should the government provide free air conditioning for all vulnerable people?
Should the UK replace "Net Zero" with a more "realistic" 70% reduction by 2070?

yes.text: Should the UK wait for other polluters (China/India) to act before doing more?
Should the UK link its own reductions legally to the global average?

no.text: Should the UK focus on cheap energy (including fracking) to build strength?
Should the UK focus on nature-based solutions (trees) rather than lifestyle change?

yes.text: Should 10% of all UK farmland be "rewilding" and taken out of production?

no.text: Should the government implement a "Frequent Flyer Levy"?

climate.name: Should new oil and gas licences be issued in UK waters
climate.text: Should the government grant new licences for North Sea oil and gas extraction?

yes.text: Should "Energy Security" (reducing imports) outweigh the climate impact?
Should companies be required to reinvest all UK profits into UK renewables?
Should the government be a "joint partner" in every new oil and gas field?
Should this revenue be used exclusively to lower bills for the poorest?

no.text: Should the government take over full ownership of resources after 2040?
Should the government "remove the windfall tax" to encourage investment?

yes.text: Should the tax only be removed if the company meets carbon targets?

no.text: Should the government instead provide tax breaks for oil sold to the UK?
Should the government only allow new licences if they are for "gas-only" fields?

yes.text: Should the UK ban the export of any gas drilled in the North Sea?
Should the government set a maximum price for this UK-only gas?

no.text: Should the government use this as a "backup" for when wind isn't blowing?
Should the government require all new platforms to be fully electrified?

yes.text: Should the government provide the initial funding for power cables?

no.text: Should companies that refuse to electrify have their licences revoked?
Should the government implement a "Total Ban" on all new North Sea exploration?

yes.text: Should the government provide a "Just Transition" fund for the 200,000 workers?
Should every worker be guaranteed a retraining grant for green energy?
Should the government also guarantee their current salary for three years?

no.text: Should the government build a new industrial hub in Aberdeen?
Should the government prioritize "Green Hydrogen" as the primary replacement?

yes.text: Should the government spend billions on a new hydrogen pipeline network?

no.text: Should the government be "legally responsible" if bills rise because of the ban?
Should the UK "import" its oil and gas from allies rather than drilling its own?

yes.text: Should the UK only import from democratic allies (Norway/US)?
Should the UK sign "20-year fixed-price" contracts for stability?

no.text: Should the government implement a carbon levy on all imported fossil fuels?
Should the UK focus on "reducing energy use" so much that no new drilling is needed?

yes.text: Should the government mandate "zero-energy" standards for buildings?

no.text: Should the government implement "energy rationing" for industry in winter?

climate.name: Should farming subsidies be tied primarily to environmental outcomes rather than food production
climate.text: Should the government prioritize environmental restoration over food production in farming subsidies?

yes.text: Should food security be maintained by focusing production on "high-yield" land?
Should "Vertical Farming" and "Lab-Grown Meat" receive the same subsidies?
Should the government provide grants for "urban vertical farms" in every city?
Should these be required to provide free food for local food banks?

no.text: Should the government implement a "meat tax" to encourage switching?
Should the government prioritize "Agro-Ecological" farming (mixing food and nature)?

yes.text: Should every farm be required by law to dedicate 10% of land to wildlife?

no.text: Should the government pay farmers to "stop using" pesticides entirely?
Should the UK accept it will "import more food" to allow nature restoration?

yes.text: Should the government only allow imports meeting UK environmental standards?
Should the government be allowed to veto trade deals hurting green goals?

no.text: Should the government provide "consumer subsidies" for sustainable food?
Should the government focus on "Carbon Farming" paid by the carbon soil absorbs?

yes.text: Should companies buy carbon credits directly from UK farmers?

no.text: Should the government have the "first right to buy" all carbon stored?
Should the primary goal of subsidies remain "maximizing domestic food production"?

yes.text: Should the government return to the "old system" based on amount produced?
Should the government set "minimum prices" for milk and grain?
Should the government be required to buy any surplus food to stop crashes?

no.text: Should the government deregulate GMOs to help farmers produce more?
Should the government focus on "Precision Farming" technology for yields?

yes.text: Should the government provide interest-free loans for GPS-guided tractors?

no.text: Should the government provide "young farmer" grants to encourage entry?
Should the government abolish all farming subsidies and let the market decide?

yes.text: Should the government remove land-use restrictions for building on farms?
Should the government still provide disaster insurance for total failure?

no.text: Should the government apply a high-carbon tariff on nitrogen fertilizers?
Should the government focus on "Community Farming" where people own land collectively?

yes.text: Should the government provide a "right to buy" for local communities?

no.text: Should the government provide allotments for every household?
